evidence: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/usp10/ns-usp10-script_tabdef documents a negative tab stop only as far-edge alignment ('Positive values represent near-edge alignment, while negative values represent far-edge alignment') without saying what width the tab character itself gets; far-edge alignment ends the following text at the stop, which needs the width of the text after the tab, and getGivenTabWidth sees only the tab position. usp10 tests/usp10.c has no SSA_TAB or SCRIPT_TABDEF use (grep count 0), so no Windows ground truth either. Undocumented algorithm AND untested; the case (cTabStops == 1 with a negative first stop) is rare. Left as the FIXME.

learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-getsystemdpiforprocess: for another process the result depends on THAT process's DPI awareness (unaware -> 96, otherwise the system DPI). Wine keeps a process's awareness only in its own win32u (dpi_context in win32u/sysparams.c); wineserver has no per-process DPI state (grep of server/protocol.def: only window and thread dpi_context), and NtUserGetProcessDpiAwarenessContext itself answers 'unaware' for other processes with a WARN. Returning 96 would be consistent with that but wrong for aware targets, so the honest fix needs the server. Proposal (design decision, wineserver protocol change = full rebuild of all unix modules): add set_process_dpi_awareness / get_process_dpi_awareness requests storing the awareness in struct process, set from NtUserSetProcessDpiAwarenessContext and read by both NtUserGetProcessDpiAwarenessContext and NtUserGetSystemDpiForProcess (unaware -> USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI, else system_dpi); needs the target process handle to have PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION.
